name: kim2017_malaria
citation: Kim D, Brown Z, Anderson R, Mutero C, Miranda ML, Wiener J, Kramer R (2017) The value of information in decision-analytic modeling for malaria vector control in East Africa. Risk Analysis 37:231-244
licence: All rights reserved (Society for Risk Analysis); only the numbers of Tables III to V are transcribed, as facts, with their source
retrieved: 2026-11-24, article PDF supplied by the user; Tables III to V compared across two text extractions and the PDF pages
decision: Which malaria vector-control programme to run for ten years in a rural East African setting: the status quo (indoor residual spraying), larviciding four or eight times a year, or spraying with larviciding
unit: net benefit in US dollars per person over ten years, relative to the status quo (the paper's valuation: DALYs averted at 7,773 dollars each, less programme cost, discounted at 3%)

action_names.status_quo: 90% indoor residual spraying only (payoff zero: Table IV is relative to it)
action_names.larviciding_4: Alternative 1: full larviciding, 4 rounds a year
action_names.larviciding_8: Alternative 2: full larviciding, 8 rounds a year
action_names.irs_larviciding_4: Alternative 3: 90% indoor residual spraying with full larviciding, 4 rounds a year

table3.provenance: Table III: the three values chosen for each parameter and their probabilities under the lognormal distributions; low, medium, high

table4.provenance: Table IV, ex post payoffs relative to the status quo: for each case, nine scenarios (the first parameter varies slowest) by the three alternatives in the order larviciding_4, larviciding_8, irs_larviciding_4. The two parameters of a case are independent (Section 2.4)

resolution.evpi_rounding: Table V prints EVPI as the difference of the rounded prior and perfect-information values: unrounded, cases A and B are 0.38 and 4.17 where the paper prints 0.3 and 4.1.

not_replicated.reason: The uniform column of Table V (maximum EPU, EPPI, EVPI) cannot be recomputed: the probabilities of the three values under the uniform distributions are not printed. Equal thirds do not give it (case A: 92.73 and 93.29), and in case D they make Alternative 3 the best action without information, where the text says Alternative 2 always is. The payoffs themselves are outputs of the authors' model (MDAST), which is not rerun; the paper computes no single-parameter or sample information.
